source.title: Random Label Prediction Heads for Studying Memorization in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Marlon Becker; Jonas Konrad; Luis Garcia Rodriguez; Benjamin Risse

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures random-label prediction and changes memorization with an auxiliary regularizer, then reports effects on natural-label test accuracy. This conceptually tests whether memorization reduction tracks generalization, though it does not reproduce the claim versions' original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper's random-label-head measurements, width sweep, and comparisons with dropout, weight decay, and label smoothing are not evidence for versions unless they measure the version's stated outcome. Figure-only test-accuracy results for dropout are included as a row, but the text does not state their direction or exact values. Findings about random-label accuracy and model size are listed under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.15 reports full-network random-label training of WideResNet models on CIFAR-100, extending V1's capacity comparison to a new architecture and dataset. Natural-label training and held-out performance are reported elsewhere for WideResNet-16-4. Random-label held-out performance is not reported. The dropout experiment uses a transformer, outside V6's stated fully connected and convolutional classifiers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that suppressing measured memorization can improve or impair generalization depending on dataset and training setup. They propose sampling as an explanation, rather than establishing it as a universal mechanism, and report that final-layer regularization can shift memorization into earlier layers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses auxiliary random-label prediction heads and an adversarial memorization regularizer during ordinary task training; it does not use the versions' stated interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of RLP-regularization on test performance varies by dataset and setup: it improves performance on ImageNet in some settings but worsens it on CIFAR-100; on ImageNet, benefit depends on dataset fraction, and applying regularization across all layers reduces random-label accuracy without improving test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: ViT-B/32 is evaluated with varying dropout on ImageNet with 10% label noise; Appendix A.14 collectively describes test-performance improvements under the compared regularizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can affect transformer generalization under label noise; the dropout-specific direction and magnitude cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

fits_no_version.finding: Auxiliary random-label accuracy increases with network width, and depends on head capacity and the number of random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label prediction from learned representations measures a capacity-dependent property; this alone does not test post-interpolation test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing auxiliary random-label prediction improves ImageNet performance in some settings but harms CIFAR-100 performance and does not improve Yahoo! Answers performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization consequences of suppressing this memorization proxy depend on dataset, sampling, and intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet-LT, RLP-regularization lowers performance for sparsely sampled classes; no highly memorized-example removal comparison is performed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing sample-specific representations can impair rare-class generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-sample auxiliary random-label accuracy correlates weakly with Feldman-style memorization scores: Pearson's r = 0.08.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary random-label predictability and inclusion-based memorization scores capture different sample properties; their disagreement does not test V8's removal result.

record.problems: Several findings are presented only in figures without exact values or uncertainty; the study's RLP-head is a proxy for memorization whose capacity depends on the number of random labels and head design. Some results are specific to particular datasets and training setups.
record.rows_left_out: No further eligible rows for the claim versions. Numerous random-label-accuracy measurements and regularization sweeps do not measure the outcomes named by the versions; the dropout test-accuracy plot is retained as R1, with figure-only values and state cannot_determine.

untested.parts: Chance-level held-out accuracy after full-network random-label training; the original architectures and datasets. Auxiliary-head accuracy alone does not establish full-network random-label fitting.
Held-out error across widths beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Held-out optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's held-out effects in fully connected or convolutional classifiers, including small datasets, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Full-network random-label training accuracy across WideResNet widths, including near-perfect fitting at sufficient width. Record these separately from auxiliary-head accuracy; their reported correlation is r = 0.93.

Natural-label training and held-out accuracy for the unregularized WideResNet-16-4 baseline, paired with its full-network random-label result where identifiable. Exact plotted values require the figure; do not substitute auxiliary-head accuracy for full-network training accuracy.
missing.locator: Section 5.3, Figure 5 at λ = 0; Appendix A.1; Appendix A.15, Figure A.17

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says that full-network random-label training is absent; Appendix A.15 explicitly performs it. The V1 verdict concerns only the coexistence components tested here. Figure text preserves axes and captions but does not reliably preserve curves or individual values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes to fit fixed random labels and natural labels in separate runs, or report held-out chance accuracy for random labels.
The width sweep reports random-label accuracy, not test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or isolate local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not compare batch sizes or report a large-batch generalization gap.

Dropout test-accuracy outcomes are shown only in figures without text describing the direction or precise values; the paper does not test very small training sets or state that excessive dropout underfits.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.
Does not remove highly memorized examples and compare retraining with random-example removal.

rows.subject: ViT-B/32
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy while varying dropout rate in a setup with 10% label noise.
rows.note: The figure plots test accuracy by dropout rate, but the prose does not describe the direction or give values.
rows.check: ViT-B/32 is a transformer, outside V6's stated architecture classes. The correct locator is Appendix A.14, Figure A.15, not Appendix A.15. The supplied figure text does not preserve the plotted curves, so dropout-specific direction and values cannot be established.

relationships.condition: Sufficiently wide WideResNet models on CIFAR-100; random-label fitting and natural-label generalization components
relationships.reason: Based on text and figures omitted from the rows: Appendix A.15/Figure A.17 shows near-perfect full-network random-label fitting at sufficient widths, while Section 5.3/Figure 5 reports natural-label held-out performance for WideResNet-16-4. This supports coexistence, but does not establish chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: The reported near-perfect random-label fitting at sufficient widths and natural-label held-out performance remain unverified from the available source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
